Ingenio is supporting a leading international law firm with the appointment of a Global Head of Digital Strategy & Transformation
.

This is a senior leadership position reporting directly to the Global Chief Operating Officer, with significant exposure to the Board and wider executive leadership team. The successful candidate will lead the firm's digital transformation strategy, bringing together business applications, data, AI, automation and digital client services to deliver measurable business improvements.

This is not a traditional IT infrastructure or operational technology role. An established CTO is responsible for those areas. The focus of this appointment is on strategy, development, transformation and execution
.

The Opportunity
You will take responsibility for developing and delivering a global digital transformation strategy across legal, corporate and trust services. Working with senior business stakeholders, you will turn commercial and operational challenges into practical technology solutions that improve efficiency, client experience and service delivery.

You'll inherit an established application development team and will be responsible for developing its capabilities as the transformation programme progresses.

Significant projects are already underway, including a major entity-management platform initiative, a broader data management and analytics programme, and opportunities to extend the use of AI and automation across the business.

Key Responsibilities
Develop and deliver a global digital strategy and transformation roadmap aligned with business priorities.
Lead and develop the existing Business Technology and Application Development team.
Own the business applications roadmap, including entity management and client-facing technology solutions.
Oversee the design, development and delivery of new systems, whether built internally, purchased or delivered through external partners.
Drive the data strategy, analytics, reporting and business intelligence agenda.
Identify and implement practical AI and automation opportunities across legal and professional services.

What We're Looking For
We are particularly interested in senior digital transformation and business technology leaders from professional services, legal, fiduciary/corporate services, financial services or similarly complex, regulated environments
.

You will bring:
Significant experience leading digital strategy, business technology or enterprise transformation.
A proven track record of delivering complex technology programmes with measurable business outcomes.
Strong experience across business applications, software development and technology-enabled process improvement.
A solid understanding of data strategy, analytics, business intelligence, AI and automation.
Experience leading multidisciplinary development teams and managing external delivery partners.
The ability to influence Board-level stakeholders while remaining technically credible and close to delivery.

Location & Package
Toronto is the mandatory location, with this being an in-office role.

Interested?
This is an opportunity to shape the digital direction of an established international professional services organisation, with direct access to senior leadership, an existing development capability and significant transformation programmes already underway.

For a confidential discussion, please contact Michelle Queally at Ingenio
, or apply directly.

About Us

At CSDS, we prioritize people
—both within our team and in the communities we serve. Our mission is to redefine how Nova Scotians engage with government by creating accessible, reliable digital solutions centered around user needs.

In today’s tech-driven world, CSDS empowers government departments with essential digital solutions to meet Nova Scotians’ expectations.
As a trusted partner across government, we enable departments to fulfill their mandates with secure, user-friendly services. From healthcare and education to public safety, we collaborate to transform how services are designed and delivered.

We don’t just implement technology; we modernize outdated systems and reimagine processes.
Our agile, data-driven approach ensures that digital services are both efficient and adaptable to Nova Scotia’s evolving needs.

Joining CSDS means contributing to work that makes a real difference.
From providing vital tech support to healthcare professionals to strengthening cybersecurity and developing scalable digital platforms, you’ll play a key role in building a more inclusive, responsive government for Nova Scotians.

Together, we’re setting new standards for digital public service, delivering resilient solutions that meet today’s needs—and anticipate tomorrow’s challenges.

About Our Opportunity

Are you a collaborative, forward-looking leader who can turn complex health-system needs into clear digital pathways and better outcomes? Digital Solutions helps health initiatives move safely from early idea through design, review, approval, implementation, and production readiness. The team works across CSDS, Nova Scotia Health, IWK Health, the Department of Health and Wellness, vendors, and other partners to shape solution design, strengthen architecture and governance, reduce risk, and coordinate dependencies across the broader digital health environment.

As Director, Digital Solutions, you will provide strategic and operational leadership for the team responsible for digital-health intake, business analysis, solution architecture, service navigation, and early delivery enablement. Reporting to the Executive Director of Digital Health Enablement, you will create the conditions for multidisciplinary teams to deliver secure, scalable, user-centred solutions that support clinical care, health-system transformation, and improved experiences for patients, providers, and partners.

You will bring structure to ambiguity, establish trusted relationships, and ensure initiatives receive timely guidance on technical design, architecture review, security and privacy alignment, procurement, operational readiness, and enterprise dependencies. Your leadership will help partners make informed decisions earlier, prevent avoidable redesign, and move priority work forward with greater clarity and confidence.

Primary Accountabilities

Provide senior leadership and oversight for the Digital Solutions portfolio, setting clear priorities and ensuring work is aligned with departmental, health-system, and enterprise objectives.
Lead and support managers, solution architects, business analysts, and other multidisciplinary resources, creating an empowered, inclusive, accountable, and delivery-focused team culture.
Oversee the intake, assessment, and early shaping of digital-health initiatives, ensuring partners receive practical guidance to define needs, clarify outcomes, identify dependencies, and determine the appropriate delivery and approval pathway.
Guide initiatives through solution design, architecture review, security and privacy alignment, procurement and contractual considerations, implementation planning, production readiness, and transition to operational support.
Provide advice and recommendations to the Executive Director Digital Health Enablement and senior government and health-system leaders, translating complex technical, delivery, financial, and operational issues into clear options, risks, and decisions.
Build and maintain strong partnerships across CSDS, Nova Scotia Health, IWK Health, the Department of Health and Wellness, other public-sector organisations, vendors, and jurisdictional partners.
Ensure effective portfolio governance, including prioritisation, risk and issue management, escalation, performance visibility, resource planning, and accountability for commitments.
Champion human-centred, iterative, and continuous-improvement approaches, helping teams adopt modern digital practices and respond effectively to changing requirements.
Work collaboratively to identify opportunities for innovation, reuse, standardisation, automation, and increased value across the digital-health ecosystem.
Provide sound stewardship of human and financial resources, including workforce planning, performance management, budget oversight, forecasting, procurement support, and value-for-money recommendations.
Represent Digital Health Enablement in governance forums, partner engagements, working groups, and cross-sector planning activities, promoting a connected and system-wide approach to digital-health delivery.

How You Can Make An Impact

Enable safer and more effective digital-health delivery by engaging early, resolving uncertainty, and reducing downstream risk and rework.
Improve the end-to-end partner experience by making CSDS pathways, requirements, decisions, and accountabilities easier to understand and navigate.
Help major health initiatives move from concept to implementation with stronger alignment across technology, clinical needs, operations, security, privacy, procurement, and vendors.
Build an engaged team that is trusted for its judgement, responsiveness, collaboration, and ability to create a practical path forward.
Advance digital enablement that contributes to better healthcare experiences and outcomes for Nova Scotians.

Qualifications And Experience

You are a credible and collaborative people leader with strategic leadership experience and a demonstrated record of delivery in complex environments. You are comfortable working across executive, operational, clinical, business, and technical settings, and you can translate competing needs into focused action.

Progressive leadership experience in digital delivery, information technology, health informatics, service transformation, business analysis, enterprise or solution architecture, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary and cross-functional teams, including internal employees, external resources, partners, and vendors.
Experience overseeing a portfolio of complex initiatives and balancing strategic priorities, operational pressures, delivery risk, and changing requirements.
A strong understanding of digital solutions and how technology, data, architecture, security, privacy, procurement, and operations come together to enable sustainable services.
Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships and bring together diverse partners to reach constructive outcomes.
Experience providing clear, concise, and evidence-informed advice to senior leaders and decision-making bodies.
Experience with governance, prioritisation, risk management, financial stewardship, resource planning, vendor management, and service improvement.
Knowledge of modern digital and internet-era practices, including human-centred design, agile and iterative delivery, product or service thinking, and continuous improvement.
Excellent communication, facilitation, negotiation, and presentation skills, with the ability to make complex information accessible to varied audiences.
Demonstrated commitment to service excellence, respect, integrity, diversity, accountability, and the public good.

An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered. Experience in healthcare, digital health, government, or another complex regulated environment would be considered an asset.

About GrandBridge Corporation

Who We Are:

GrandBridge Corporation is an investment holding company dedicated to driving growth and innovation through our fully owned subsidiaries, GrandBridge Energy Inc., and GrandBridge Group Inc.

GrandBridge Energy Inc. is a leading provider of innovative energy solutions, committed to delivering reliable and sustainable energy to our customers. GrandBridge Group Inc. offers a wide range of energy services through its divisions: Netoptiks, which provides cutting-edge telecommunications solutions, and Enersure, which ensures our customers' homes are comfortable and energy-efficient with home comfort rentals.

Our team of dedicated professionals are committed to helping our communities navigate the transition towards a dynamic and evolving energy landscape. The principles and beliefs that guide our operations are deeply rooted in our values. Join us in our mission to shape the future of energy.

What We Offer

Employer Paid Benefits Package
OMERS Pension Plan
Training and Educational Reimbursement Programs
Professional Development & Career Opportunities
Wellness Resources & Healthy Lifestyle Incentives
Employee and Family Assistance Program
Opportunities for Community Involvement

About The Role:

As the Vice President, Finance & Chief Financial Officer (CFO), you will be a key member of the Executive Leadership team, reporting directly to the President & CEO. You will provide strategic leadership and executive oversight for finance, accounting, business and financial planning, treasury, tax, enterprise risk management, investor relations and procurement, while serving as a trusted advisor to the President & CEO, Board of Directors, and Executive Leadership team.

You will play a critical role in shaping the Corporation’s financial strategy, long-term sustainability, and overall business performance. As the Corporation’s senior financial executive, you will lead the development and execution of financial strategies that support growth across both regulated and competitive businesses, while ensuring sound governance, prudent risk management, disciplined capital allocation, and strong financial stewardship.

The Vice President, Finance & CFO will also play a significant role in evaluating mergers and acquisitions, strategic partnerships, and other significant investment opportunities, providing financial leadership and insight to support the Corporation’s growth strategy.

We are seeking an accomplished and forward-thinking leader with the strategic insight, financial acumen, and executive presence to help guide the Corporation through a period of continued growth and transformation. The successful candidate will be a collaborative and trusted partner who builds strong relationships, influences complex decisions, and leads with integrity, accountability, and a commitment to excellence. You will foster a high-performing, engaged team while advancing a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, and exceptional service to customers, stakeholders, and the communities we serve.

What You Will Do:

Strategic Leadership & Business Performance
:
Partner with the President & CEO, Corporate Development and Executive Leadership team to shape and execute our growth strategy across regulated and competitive businesses.
Provide strategic advice on enterprise strategy, capital deployment, growth, risk and financial implications of major decisions.
Lead financial strategies that support sustainable growth, operational excellence, and long-term value creation.
Align financial plans, resources, funding plans, and performance measures with corporate priorities.
Develop decision frameworks, scenarios, and performance insights that improve the quality and speed of Executive and Board decisions.
Champion accountability, innovation, continuous improvement, and data-driven decision-making.

Growth, M&A, and Competitive Business Development

Lead the financial evaluation of acquisitions, mergers, partnerships, joint ventures, new markets and business opportunities.
Develop transaction and financing structures that balance strategic value, financial returns, tax, regulatory requirements, and overall capital capacity.
Serve as a strategic partner by strengthening business models, pricing, investment governance, performance measures and scalable financial capabilities that support profitable growth.
Co-lead transaction integration and post-investment oversight, including financial systems, controls, cost allocation, synergy tracking and benefits realization, ensuring that approved investments deliver sustainable enterprise value.

Financial Stewardship and Transformation

Provide executive leadership for all finance, accounting and financial planning functions.
Ensure the integrity, accuracy and timeliness of consolidated and operating entity financial reporting, accounting, management information, and external disclosures.
Modernize finance systems, processes, data and analytics to improve efficiency, automation, forecasting accuracy, decision support and the scalability required for business growth and future acquisitions.
Maintain a strong system of internal control, delegated authority, financial policy and assurance that protects the company’s assets and reputation.
Lead enterprise budgeting, forecasting, and performance reporting, providing the President & CEO, Boards and Executive Leadership team with clear, forward-looking insights, and early identification of emerging risks and opportunities.
Support the Corporation’s ESG objectives through financial leadership, performance measurement, reporting, and decision support.

Treasury, Risk Management & Investor Relations:

Lead treasury, financing, liquidity, and capital structure strategies.
Manage effective relationships with municipal shareholders, lenders, rating agencies, and other key financial stakeholders.
Provide executive oversight of the Enterprise Risk Management framework.
Ensure that strategic, financial, transaction and emerging risks are identified, assessed and integrated into capital allocation, business planning, and executive decision making.
Oversee tax planning, compliance, and reporting activities.

Regulatory Affairs:

Advise the President & CEO, Executive Leadership Team and Boards on the financial, strategic and enterprise implications of regulatory policy, emerging requirements and industry developments, identifying opportunities, risks and recommended actions.
Translate regulatory decisions, commitments and emerging policy directions into the financial plans, capital strategy, forecasts, performance measures and risk-management priorities.
Provide executive-level financial leadership for major rate applications, capital funding mechanisms and regulatory initiatives, ensuring that revenue requirements, forecasts, cost allocation, and capital plans are credible, integrated and financially sustainable.
Lead engagement and advocacy with regulators, governments, sector organizations and other stakeholders to advance regulatory frameworks that enable innovation, investments, and improved outcomes for customers and communities.
Partner with General Counsel to integrate and align financial, legal, policy and regulatory perspectives in applications, advocacy, compliance and business development.

Procurement & Supply Chain:

Provide executive leadership and oversight for procurement and supply chain strategy.
Lead the transformation and integration of procurement and supply-chain capabilities, including processes, systems, data, analytics and supplier governance.
Establish procurement policies, controls, authorities, and performance measures and ensure procurement practices support value, transparency, compliance, and prudent risk management.
Promote strategic sourcing, supplier performance management, and continuous improvement.
Partner with business leaders to strengthen commercial decision-making and contract management.

What You Will Bring

Graduate degree in Commerce, Finance, Business, or related discipline, with a CPA designation.
Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience in finance or accounting, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership or executive role.
Strong expertise in financial planning, accounting, treasury, capital management, enterprise risk management, and business performance.

Experience in the energy, utility, or other capital-intensive sector is preferred. Knowledge of the regulated business environment and regulatory processes is an asset.
Demonstrated success leading and developing high-performing teams while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, engagement, and continuous improvement.
Proven ability to influence senior leaders and Boards, applying sound judgment, critical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills to complex business issues.
Strong executive presence and the ability to build credibility and effective relationships with employees, executives, directors, regulators, financial institutions, and other key stakeholders.
Excellent communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to convey complex financial and business matters to diverse audiences.

jobs.title: Interim Director Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.description:
IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Director Financial Planning and Analysis

Reports: Vice President Finance

Duration: 3 Months

Location: Toronto

Hybrid Work (2 – 3 Days onsite)

The Opportunity

This is an exciting opportunity for an accomplished FP&A leader to step into a large, complex Canadian not-for-profit organization at a critical point in its annual financial planning cycle.

Following a recent departure, the organization requires an experienced Interim Director of Financial Planning & Analysis to provide immediate leadership to an established, high-performing team and successfully steer the organization through a complex and evolving budgeting process.

This is not a "blow it up and rebuild it" assignment. The foundations are strong, the team is capable, and significant work is already underway. The mandate is about bringing experienced, steady leadership, maintaining momentum and getting the very best from the people, processes, technology and financial information already in place.

A major focus will be optimizing the use of Excel, and existing financial reporting tools to provide stronger modelling, analysis and insight throughout the budgeting process. The successful interim will help ensure that a new budgeting approach and supporting technology are effectively embedded while giving senior leadership confidence in the integrity, quality and usefulness of the organization's financial information.

The Mandate

The Interim Director, Financial Planning & Analysis will take immediate leadership of the FP&A function during a particularly important period for the organization.
Key priorities will include:
Lead and support an established, high-performing FP&A team through a period of leadership transition.
Own and drive a critical organization-wide budgeting and forecasting process, ensuring key milestones, deliverables and timelines are achieved.
Provide strong financial leadership as the organization works through a new budgeting process and associated technology.
Optimize the use of Excel, Power BI and existing reporting platforms to strengthen financial modelling, analysis, reporting and decision support.
Develop and enhance sophisticated financial models to support budgeting, forecasting, scenario planning and organizational decision-making.
Ensure senior executives and operational leaders receive clear, timely and actionable financial information throughout the budgeting cycle.
Support business leaders in understanding budgets, assumptions, variances, risks and financial implications across their respective areas.
Bring together financial information across multiple entities and business areas, ensuring accurate and meaningful consolidated reporting.
Identify practical opportunities to improve the use of existing systems and reporting capabilities without introducing unnecessary disruption or change.
Maintain strong financial discipline and consistency across the budgeting and forecasting process.
Partner closely with senior finance leadership and other organizational stakeholders, providing informed analysis, constructive challenge and practical financial advice.
Coach and support the FP&A team, maintaining engagement, accountability and confidence during the transition.

Technology, Data & Insights

A key component of this assignment will be helping the organization get more value from its existing technology and financial information.

The successful interim will be comfortable working in a technology-enabled finance environment and will bring particular strength in:

Advanced Excel-based financial modelling and analysis.
Power BI dashboards, analytics and management reporting.
Budgeting and forecasting systems.
ERP and financial reporting platforms.
Multi-entity financial reporting and consolidation.
Scenario modelling and sensitivity analysis.
Systems implementation, adoption and optimization.
Translating complex financial data into meaningful management insight.
The individual does not need to be a technology specialist. They do, however, need to understand how technology, data and financial modelling can be used to make FP&A faster, more insightful and more valuable to organizational decision makers.

What Success Looks Like

Build financial models, support commercial lender relationships, assess capital needs, conduct financial due diligence on M&A targets, and establish a repeatable playbook for onboarding new acquisitions into the group platform.

Interim Director Financial Planning and Analysis

Reports: Vice President Finance

Duration: 3 Months

Location: Toronto

Hybrid Work (2 – 3 Days onsite)

The Opportunity

This is an exciting opportunity for an accomplished FP&A leader to step into a large, complex Canadian not-for-profit organization at a critical point in its annual financial planning cycle.

Following a recent departure, the organization requires an experienced Interim Director of Financial Planning & Analysis to provide immediate leadership to an established, high-performing team and successfully steer the organization through a complex and evolving budgeting process.

This is not a "blow it up and rebuild it" assignment. The foundations are strong, the team is capable, and significant work is already underway. The mandate is about bringing experienced, steady leadership, maintaining momentum and getting the very best from the people, processes, technology and financial information already in place.

A major focus will be optimizing the use of Excel, and existing financial reporting tools to provide stronger modelling, analysis and insight throughout the budgeting process. The successful interim will help ensure that a new budgeting approach and supporting technology are effectively embedded while giving senior leadership confidence in the integrity, quality and usefulness of the organization's financial information.

The Mandate

The Interim Director, Financial Planning & Analysis will take immediate leadership of the FP&A function during a particularly important period for the organization.
Key priorities will include:
Lead and support an established, high-performing FP&A team through a period of leadership transition.
Own and drive a critical organization-wide budgeting and forecasting process, ensuring key milestones, deliverables and timelines are achieved.
Provide strong financial leadership as the organization works through a new budgeting process and associated technology.
Optimize the use of Excel, Power BI and existing reporting platforms to strengthen financial modelling, analysis, reporting and decision support.
Develop and enhance sophisticated financial models to support budgeting, forecasting, scenario planning and organizational decision-making.
Ensure senior executives and operational leaders receive clear, timely and actionable financial information throughout the budgeting cycle.
Support business leaders in understanding budgets, assumptions, variances, risks and financial implications across their respective areas.
Bring together financial information across multiple entities and business areas, ensuring accurate and meaningful consolidated reporting.
Identify practical opportunities to improve the use of existing systems and reporting capabilities without introducing unnecessary disruption or change.
Maintain strong financial discipline and consistency across the budgeting and forecasting process.
Partner closely with senior finance leadership and other organizational stakeholders, providing informed analysis, constructive challenge and practical financial advice.
Coach and support the FP&A team, maintaining engagement, accountability and confidence during the transition.

Technology, Data & Insights

A key component of this assignment will be helping the organization get more value from its existing technology and financial information.

The successful interim will be comfortable working in a technology-enabled finance environment and will bring particular strength in:

Advanced Excel-based financial modelling and analysis.
Power BI dashboards, analytics and management reporting.
Budgeting and forecasting systems.
ERP and financial reporting platforms.
Multi-entity financial reporting and consolidation.
Scenario modelling and sensitivity analysis.
Systems implementation, adoption and optimization.
Translating complex financial data into meaningful management insight.
The individual does not need to be a technology specialist. They do, however, need to understand how technology, data and financial modelling can be used to make FP&A faster, more insightful and more valuable to organizational decision makers.

What Success Looks Like

At the conclusion of the three-month assignment, the organization should have:
Successfully navigated a critical budgeting cycle.
Maintained stability, engagement and performance within an already strong FP&A team.
Embedded and optimized the organization's new budgeting process and supporting technology.
Increased confidence in budgeting, forecasting and management reporting.
Improved financial modelling and scenario-planning capabilities.
Better utilization of Excel, Power BI and existing financial reporting tools.
Clearer consolidated reporting across a complex, multi-entity environment.
Stronger financial insight available to senior leadership to support decision-making.
A well-positioned FP&A function ready for the next stage of its development.

Ideal Background

The ideal candidate will bring:

Significant experience leading Financial Planning & Analysis within a large, complex not-for-profit organization.
Previous experience within the not-for-profit, healthcare, broader public sector, association, social services or another complex mission-driven environment.
A recognized accounting designation, MBA in Finance or equivalent senior-level financial qualification and experience.
Demonstrated experience leading and developing established finance and FP&A teams.
Strong expertise in complex budgeting, forecasting and long-range financial planning.
Advanced Excel financial modelling capabilities.
Strong experience with Power BI and other management-reporting and visualization tools.
Experience working with ERP, budgeting and financial reporting platforms, including system implementation, adoption or optimization.
Experience with multi-entity environments and consolidated financial reporting is highly desirable.
Strong analytical capability with the ability to move beyond reporting numbers to explaining what they mean and what leadership should do about them.
Experience working with senior executives and operational leaders in organizations with multiple stakeholders, competing priorities and significant complexity.

This is an assignment for someone who can quickly establish credibility, support a strong team, roll up their sleeves when required and confidently navigate senior stakeholders through a complex budgeting process.

Above all, they will know how to use FP&A for what it should ultimately be: not simply producing budgets and reports, but giving leaders the financial insight, foresight and confidence to make better decisions.

Full-time | Active New Vacancy

Ottawa, Ontario preferred | Remote work available with periodic travel to Ottawa

About the Role

Ottawa Physiotherapy & Sports Clinic is executing a multi-site clinic integration strategy, bringing several independently owned clinics under a unified corporate framework and building the foundational infrastructure to scale over time. We are seeking a hands-on, growth-oriented Director of Finance to unify distributed clinical financial operations, deliver clear visibility on consolidated cash flow and performance to executive leadership, and partner on the execution of our corporate growth strategy.

You will spearhead the financial integration roadmap with direct support from clinic owners and the executive leadership team. This mandate requires working closely with clinic leaders to design workflows that balance local clinic realities with parent-company governance, collaborating tightly with operations management where system changes intersect with clinic workflows.

What You’ll Lead

Finance Operations and Controls:
Oversee accounting, budgeting, forecasting, cash optimization, and financial reporting across all corporate entities. Standardize clinic-level workflows for payments, collections, reconciliations, and internal approvals. Manage relationships with external advisors for year-end preparation, corporate tax compliance, and regulatory reporting.
Systems Integration & Efficiency:
Lead the evaluation, selection, and implementation of a shared corporate finance platforms. Oversee data migration, training, and system adoption. Identify and execute cost and time saving opportunities through centralized vendor purchasing and shared processes.
Change Leadership & Stakeholder Management:
Act as a trusted financial partner to legacy clinic owners. Guide clinic teams through the cultural shift of financial centralization, ensuring clear communication regarding the purpose of new controls, governance, and standardized policies without causing friction in clinical workflows.
Financing, Acquisitions, and Growth:
Partner with executive leadership to plan and model funding future growth. Build financial models, support commercial lender relationships, assess capital needs, conduct financial due diligence on M&A targets, and establish a repeatable playbook for onboarding new acquisitions into the group platform.

What You Bring

15+ years of progressive finance or accounting leadership experience, with a proven track record of managing reporting, cash flow, and financial controls across multiple locations, legal entities, or distributed operating units.
Demonstrated experience leading financial system migrations, cloud ERP implementations, or standardizing fragmented workflows into a centralized shared-services model.
Strong communication and change-management skills, with the ability to translate complex financial concepts into actionable insights for clinical owners and stakeholders, and encourage adoption of new ways of working.
A university degree in accounting, finance, business administration, or a related discipline (or equivalent professional experience).
Experience in clinic practice roll-ups, mergers & acquisitions, or post-acquisition integration, preferably in a private healthcare clinic or multi-site service business, is highly valued. A CPA designation (CA, CMA, CGA) is strongly preferred.

Your First 90 Days

First 30 Days:
Assess each clinic’s legacy accounting software, billing and collections mechanisms, banking structures, and reporting tools. Establish a standardized baseline for localized cash flow, identify immediate operational or compliance risks, and align with leadership on the centralization sequence.
Days 31–60:
Begin centralizing priority finance functions, including corporate cash visibility, vendor payments, and consolidated reporting. Establish a unified corporate chart of accounts, standardized approval processes, and a rigorous month-end close calendar. Define the functional requirements for a shared cloud ERP/finance system and finalize the rollout timeline.
Days 61–90:
Deploy consolidated management reporting, clinic-level performance dashboards, and an agile group cash forecasting model. Begin the phased rollout of the shared finance systems across locations, clearly communicating milestones for completed work. Leverage the financial baseline to collaborate with leadership on a multi-year growth plan, including funding needs and acquisition priorities.

Location and Compensation

Base Salary Range:
$160,000 – $200,000 CAD per annum (commensurate with experience).
Additional Benefits:
Eligibility for a performance bonus tied to corporate and individual growth milestones, along with an opportunity to participate in the company's equity arrangement.
Work Arrangement:
Full-time. Ottawa-based candidates are preferred. Remote flexibility is available, with the expectation of periodic travel to Ottawa (approximately 2–3 days per month during peak initial integration phases, scaling to a quarterly cadence thereafter).

How to Apply

To apply, please forward your résumé to recruitment@optsc.com. Please include a brief summary or example of a multi-site finance integration or systems rollout you previously executed and the operational outcomes achieved.

Please note that Ottawa Physiotherapy & Sports Clinic does not utilize automated AI-driven screening or algorithmic ranking software to evaluate applicants for this position. All resumes and applications are reviewed manually by our internal recruitment team.
